title: SRDF v4 (with EasyEnsemble candidate) is outperformed by EasyEnsemble standalone: the Arbiter harms on 11% of cases.
interpretation: When a strong candidate (EasyEnsemble) is available, the SRDF Arbiter systematically underperforms it. The Arbiter selects the strong candidate in 88.83% of cases, but on the remaining 11% (67 cases) it selects a weaker candidate and loses 8.52 pp relative to always-choosing EE. This is a fundamental limitation of utility-based runtime arbitration when a dominant candidate exists.

implications.for_framework: The Arbiter needs a "when to arbitrate" gate. A trivial baseline (always-select-highest-mean-candidate) outperforms the Arbiter on this cohort.
implications.for_paper: This becomes the central negative result. Combined with v1-v2-v3 positive progression, it tells a complete story: Arbiter helps on comparable candidates, harms on dominant ones.
implications.for_future_work: S07 should investigate: (a) per-candidate calibration, (b) abstention mechanism, (c) candidate-specific thresholds.
